pairs.rule: Edited-model accuracy at a stated edit norm follows the base plus the flat random-edit curve: on hard328 with the cue (T 1.0, one sample, seed 3000000) the base scores 164 and random rank-8 edits at sizes -1 to 3 (incl. two draws at 1.5x) score 152-167, mean about 160 with sd about 4, so any norm-matched 1.5x edit whose content I may not use gets about 160 with an interval of single-sample noise plus allowance for subspace structure (m smaller = more concentrated edit = slightly wider low tail); vote-over-k accuracy of the untrained cued base follows a log-k curve fitted to its own board points on the 328 (159.5 at 1, 188.5 at 4, 197 at 6, which fit vote(k)=159.5+20.9 ln k exactly) and checked on the stored explore-half rows (vote over 4 of samples 0-3 = 94 of 164, x2 = 188), with interval width from tie-breaking noise measured on those rows (plus or minus 5 on the half) and per-sample noise.

Accuracy of any edited base model comes from the untrained cued base's single-sample level on hard328 plus the spread of random weight edits at the stated norm (random rank-8 edits at sizes -1 to 3 score 158-167 of 328 with seed noise of about 5), so an edit whose content I may not use is forecast at the random-edit/base level with an interval covering that spread plus one-sample noise and some extra room for a norm concentrated in an m-dimensional subspace (m/d = 64/4096 or 8/4096); vote-over-k counts of the cued base come from its own vote curve on the 328 (159.5 at k=1, 188.5 at k=4, 197 at k=6, rising roughly linearly in ln k at about 21 problems per unit ln k, flattening the way MATH-500's curve did), extrapolated to k=8, and a vote-8 minus vote-4 gap is that extrapolation minus the k=4 point.

Base-model vote targets follow the cued base's own vote-over-k curve on the 328 (vote over 4 = 188.5 and over 6 = 197, result-c065a6), extended to k = 8 with the shape of the cued base's vote curve on MATH-500 computed from the stored 12-sample rows (explore half, mean over random k-subsets: 446.9 at 4, 456.6 at 6, 461.3 at 8, so the 6->8 step is 0.485 of the 4->6 step and the 8-4 gap is 1.485 times it), with intervals set by seed noise (one-sample seeds differ by up to 9 problems). An edit's accuracy at a given edit norm follows the cued base's one-sample score plus the slope in edit norm fitted on the random rank-8 edits of the same norm family on hard328 (sizes -1 to 3: 159, 158, 159, 167, 163 against base 164, i.e. flat, slope about 0); the subspace dimension m (chance overlap m/4096) is used only to widen the interval downward for the smaller m, since a fixed norm packed into fewer residual dimensions can damage outputs; nothing about the RL change enters.

adversary.reason: The norm-1.5x edit gets base 164 plus the random-edit norm slope (flat; random edits average 161.2), so about 162, with one-sample seed noise of about 4-5 problems setting the interval.

target.what: How many of the 328 hard problems does the untrained Olmo 3 base with the opening cue get right by plurality vote over 8 samples per problem?

reader-1.reason: The base's vote curve on the 328 is 159.5/188.5/197 at k=1/4/6 (result-c065a6), still rising about 4 per sample, so k=8 should land a few problems above 197.

reader-2.reason: Vote over 6 gave 197 (188.5 at 4) and the curve flattens because most wrong problems have no right sample, so 8 samples adds about 3.

account.reason: Account S5 (the vote gains on hard328 only through scattered wrong answers, and most misses have no right sample, so about 9 points stay out of inference reach): the stored curve 159.5/188.5/197 at k=1/4/6 (result-c065a6) extrapolates log-linearly to 202 at k=8, trimmed for saturation because 107 of 131 wrong problems have no right sample among 6.

adversary.reason: vote(k)=159.5+20.9 ln k fits the 1, 4, 6 points exactly and gives 203 at k=8, which is 197 plus about 6 from the two extra samples; the interval comes from tie-breaking and per-sample noise.

account.reason: Account S5-S6 (votes help the base through scattered slips, but most of RL's vote wins on hard328 have no right base sample) means the cued-base vote curve keeps rising but flattens: 188.5 at 4 and 197 at 6 (result-c065a6), and a posterior-predictive simulation on the stored explore rows (day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2) gives about +4 for 6 to 8, so about 201.

adversary.reason: The slope is about 21 per unit ln k from k=1 to 6; flattened to about 17 that gives 17 x ln(8/6) = +5 over 197, so about 202, with plus or minus 8 for the two new samples and tie handling.

account.reason: Account S4-S5 (votes only help where the base already writes a right sample, and wrong answers scatter): the base-cue vote curve on the 328 is 159.5 at 1, 188.5 at 4 and 197 at 6 (result-c065a6), and 107 of the 131 misses have no right sample in 6, so samples 7-8 add about 2 problems each, giving about 201, still below RL's 224.

adversary.reason: 197 + 0.485 x (197 - 188.5) = 201, the 6->8 step scaled from the base's MATH-500 vote curve.

account.reason: Account S5 (the vote gains on hard328 only through scattered wrong answers, and most misses have no right sample, so about 9 points stay out of inference reach): the stored curve 159.5/188.5/197 at k=1/4/6 (result-c065a6) extrapolates log-linearly to 202 at k=8, trimmed for saturation because 107 of 131 wrong problems have no right sample among 6.

adversary.reason: vote(k)=159.5+20.9 ln k fits the 1, 4, 6 points exactly and gives 203 at k=8, which is 197 plus about 6 from the two extra samples; the interval comes from tie-breaking and per-sample noise.

target.unit: right answers of 328, vote over 8 minus vote over 4
target.what: On the 328 hard problems, for the untrained Olmo 3 base with the opening cue, how many more problems does a plurality vote over 8 samples get right than a vote over 4 samples?

reader-1.reason: Vote over 8 (~200) minus vote over 4 (188.5 subset mean, or 192 in stored order) gives roughly 8-12.

reader-2.reason: Vote over 4 is 188.5-192 depending on which four, against about 200 at 8.

account.reason: Account S5 saturation applied to result-c065a6: vote over 4 is 188.5 and the log-linear step of ~14 per doubling of k (29 over k=1 to 4, 8.5 over k=4 to 6) is shrunk by the base having no right sample on most missed problems (knowledge-b19faf: 7 % per-sample rate on 0-of-4 problems), giving about +11.5.

adversary.reason: 203 from the log-k fit minus 188.5 for the vote over 4 gives about 14; the wide interval covers which 4-sample vote is used and the tie-breaking noise.

account.reason: Same account S5-S6 vote curve: the vote over 8 at about 201 minus the vote over 4 at 188.5 (result-c065a6), with the stored explore-row simulation giving roughly +12 from 4 to 8 samples.

adversary.reason: Vote over 8 (about 202) minus a vote-over-4 point of about 190 (votek's 188.5, with room for the stored-order 192) gives about 12; the interval covers which k=4 tie rule is used and the noise from the new samples.

account.reason: Account S4 (vote turns sometimes-right into right), with gains shrinking as the base's reach saturates (S5; knowledge-b19faf: 7% per-sample rate on 0-of-4 problems): about 201 for the vote over 8 minus 188.5 for the vote over 4 (result-c065a6) gives about +12.

adversary.reason: 1.485 x 8.5 = 12.6 if the vote over 4 is averaged over subsets, 9 if it is samples 0-3 (192), so 12 with an interval covering both readings.
